# Så ska ”Snåljåpen” slå indexfonderna

**Feed**: dagen-med-di  
**Published**: 2026-09-17  
**Market Sentiment**: Positive

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Olle Kvarnström joins as a guest to present Proteon's newly launched Aktiesparfond Global, which starts with about SEK 200m. His pitch is that global index funds have become heavily concentrated in US mega-cap tech (Mag7), and he offers a cheaper actively managed alternative that picks companies one at a time. His preferred companies control their own destiny, carry little debt and have no heavy exposure to a single commodity. He is broadly positive on AI but tries to pick companies that won't lose from it rather than guess the winners: he favours TSMC, Microsoft and Assa Abloy and is sceptical of Meta's AI capex. The co-host (Micke) pushes back that beating the index by underweighting Mag7 is hard, since those companies have taken over most corners of daily life.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 ASSA-B — Assa Abloy | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 75%

Guest fund manager holds Assa Abloy: dominant, stable global company with a large aftermarket and strong cash flow.

#### Reasoning

Guest (Olle Kvarnström, fund manager) opinion. Assa Abloy fits his main test of controlling its own destiny: products everywhere worldwide, very dominant, demand not expected to fall, the aftermarket is a large share of the business, and cash flow is good. It is the Swedish name he has clearly 'taken a liking to'. He admits to a possible home bias (both he and Assa come from Eskilstuna).

#### Sell Triggers

- if structural demand for locks/access products declines
- if aftermarket share or cash flow weakens
- if leverage rises materially

> *"Det är ett typiskt bolag som jag tycker kontrollerar sitt eget öde ur ett längre perspektiv."*

---

### 🟢 TSM — TSMC | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Guest holds TSMC as a company that won't lose from AI; so many chip paths run through it, including future physical AI and robotics.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. Instead of picking AI winners, he picks companies unlikely to lose. With AI use and chip production growing, and physical AI/robotics still barely started, much of the demand passes through TSMC. He accepts the risks the host raised: Taiwan, the chip cycle, a few large customers and possible competition.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Taiwan geopolitical risk escalates
- if semiconductor cycle turns sharply
- if competitors erode foundry dominance
- if AI chip demand stalls

> *"Vem tror jag inte förlorar? Och jag tror inte att TSMC är en av de som förlorar."*

---

### 🟢 MSFT — Microsoft | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Guest is comfortable with Microsoft's heavy data-center capex because of its B2B customer base and promising demand.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. He contrasts Microsoft with Meta: Microsoft's AI capex rests on existing enterprise customers with real demand, so the spending looks well placed. It is implied to be one of the Mag7 names he holds, but below index weight.

#### Sell Triggers

- if B2B AI demand fails to materialise
- if capex returns disappoint

> *"Så när Microsoft gör enorma capexinvesteringar i datacenter, då är jag inte riktigt lika orolig för att de sitter på de kundstockarna som har den efterfrågan"*

---

### ⛔ META — Meta | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Guest is sceptical of Meta making similar huge AI capex without a B2B customer base; not a 'fun bet' to take.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. Meta spends on AI at a similar scale to Microsoft but lacks enterprise customers to monetise it, which makes the return on capex less certain. He did not say outright whether he holds it.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Meta shows clear monetisation of AI capex
- if Meta builds a B2B AI revenue stream

> *"tittar på ett Meta till exempel som gör enorma liknande investeringar som inte sitter på samma business-to-business kundkrets, då är jag inte riktigt lika säker på att det är ett kul ett kul bett att ta."*

---
